prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "suppr", with the standing line "The app moved out; what remains is the writing, and a Makefile whose only real work is staging, committing, and pushing drafts." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A long bench mechanism reading left to right. At left, an open folder of manuscript pages — essay drafts, a planner sheet, an arc sheet. Three pull-handles stand above the bench, each reaching a different distance along it: the first handle drops a gate that sweeps every loose page onto the bench; the second reaches past that gate to a stamping arm that presses a short written message onto a bundled stack; the third reaches furthest, past the stamp, to a chute leaving the page and feeding a boxed repository at right. Arrows run one way only: folder to gate to stamp to chute to repository. Draw the three handles clearly nested — the longest performs all three actions, the middle two, the shortest one.

Magnified circles set beside it show A circle on the stamping arm showing the message slot with a pre-set slug sitting in it when nothing is typed. A circle on a small gate ahead of the stamp, standing permanently open, with nothing behind it. A circle on the folder showing a written exclusion list, with the writing directory struck from tracking.

Colour is used so that One accent marks the three handles that actually move material. A second accent marks the written message travelling with the bundle. A third, greyed accent marks the parts that exist but do nothing.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: Three targets that do work; three targets that do nothing; five movements in the book; five articles in the series; about fifteen essays planned.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: make add, make commit, make push, MSG, update, build, clean, lint, article-planner.md, book-arc.md, final drafts, export — each set on the handle, slot, gate, or folder it names.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: make add, make commit, make push, stage everything, write the message, send upstream, working tree, the remote, essay drafts MSG, update, lint gate, does nothing, the ignore list, articles ignored article-planner.md, book-arc.md, final drafts, export, publication schedule, five movements pushed commits, finished essays, the series, the book build, clean, lint, empty targets, nothing to compile

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Each longer handle repeats the shorter ones; Pushing stages and commits before it sends. Unnamed messages are stamped as update; The gate passes everything, unconditionally; A failed commit does not stop the run. Drafts, plan, and arc live side by side; Export holds copies of drafted pieces. Only the writing ships from here now. Three targets are declared and blank.
